trust.title: Trust center
trust.subtitle: What PredictRx knows, what it does not know, what is still to be verified, and what is only planned.
trust.disclaimer: Decision support for a clinician. Not a diagnosis tool and not a substitute for a doctor. Written to be checked, not to impress.
trust.known.title: What it knows
trust.known.hint: Records loaded in this installation, read live from the server.
trust.counts.labels: Of these, about 590 also have openFDA label text (checked on this installation, 19 Nov 2026). The rest have interaction records only, so explanations for them are limited.
trust.counts.note: These are record counts. They are not a measure of accuracy or of how complete the data is.
trust.limit.title: What it does not know
trust.limit.coverage: Public interaction data is incomplete and can contain errors. A missing record does not mean there is no interaction.
trust.limit.brands: Local brand names are covered only by a small curated sample. A name that cannot be matched is shown as unresolved and is never guessed.
trust.limit.labs: Doses, timing and the patient's full history are not assessed. In the what-if simulation, lab values and vitals do not change a severity.
trust.limit.norecord: Public data is US- and China-centric. Local products and formulations may be missing and are shown as not found.
trust.limit.synthetic: The data in this demo is synthetic, and the system has not been clinically validated.
trust.guard.title: How a warning is made checkable
trust.guard.evidence: A finding with a severity cannot be saved without a source.
trust.guard.verifier: A separate Verifier step re-checks each finding against the interaction records and labels it verified, unverified or conflict. Conflicts are shown, never hidden.
trust.guard.norecord: A medicine pair with no record is never called safe.
trust.guard.dosing: An output guardrail checks the patient card for dosing or start/stop advice and for claims of safety.
trust.guard.pii: Personal details are removed before text is sent to an AI model.
trust.guard.audit: Reading patient data, running an analysis, family views and consent changes are recorded in an audit log.
trust.sources.title: Data sources and licences
trust.sources.fda.name: openFDA drug labels (U.S. FDA)
trust.sources.fda.text: Public domain (CC0). openFDA itself warns that its data is unvalidated and must not be relied on for medical-care decisions.
trust.sources.ddinter.name: DDInter 2.0 (drug–drug interactions)
trust.sources.ddinter.text: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: non-commercial use only. Fine for this prototype with attribution; a paid product would need the authors' permission or a licensed source. DDInter itself states that the database is incomplete and may contain errors.
trust.sources.brands.name: Brand → generic sample (team-curated)
trust.sources.brands.text: A small sample made by the team. A row stays unverified until a pharmacist reviews it, and the source references for the current sheet are still being completed.
trust.pending.title: Still to be verified
trust.pending.hint: Stated plainly so nobody has to guess.
trust.pending.brands: Row-level source references, and a pharmacist's review, for the brand → generic sample.
trust.pending.eval: A test set labelled independently by a pharmacist or clinician. Until then this app quotes no accuracy figure. Measured runs, with their number of cases, are listed on the admin Evaluation page.
trust.pending.wording: Review of the Bangla clinical wording (disclaimer, severity labels, patient-facing text) by a qualified clinician or mentor.
trust.pending.clinical: Clinical validation. The system has not been tested in routine care.
trust.plan.title: Planned next
trust.plan.hint: None of these exist in this app yet.
trust.plan.brands: A larger brand → generic list, reviewed by pharmacists.
trust.plan.study: A small validation study with clinicians, reported together with its sample size.
trust.plan.licence: A licensed interaction source, or the authors' permission, for any commercial use.
trust.plan.vitals: Pulse and SpO₂ from a low-cost ESP32 sensor. The firmware and an ingest endpoint are written but are not part of this app's flow.
trust.plan.federated: Learning across hospitals without moving patient data (federated learning).
trust.plan.audio: Respiratory risk signals from voice or cough audio.
trust.plan.markets: Other South Asian markets, with local naming layers.
rq.title: Review queue
rq.subtitle: A suggested order for looking at your patients, with the reason for each.
rq.note: Suggested review order from simple rules. It is not a clinical priority and not a safety statement. A patient with no flag has not been shown to be safe.
rq.rules.title: How the order is decided
rq.rules.intro: Each patient is listed by the first rule that applies, in this order. There is no score and no AI ranking. Only a patient's latest completed analysis is used.
rq.rule.conflict: The Verifier disagreed with the interaction records on a finding (conflict).
rq.rule.major: The latest analysis has a major finding.
rq.rule.overdue: A follow-up task is past its due date.
rq.rule.unverified: The latest analysis has an unverified finding.
rq.rule.moderate: The latest analysis has a moderate finding.
rq.rule.noAnalysis: Medicines are on record but no analysis has been completed.
rq.rule.stale: The last completed analysis is {{days}} days old or older.
rq.rule.noConsent: There is no active consent on record.
rq.reason.conflict: Verifier conflict in the latest analysis ({{n}})
rq.reason.major: Major finding in the latest analysis ({{n}})
rq.reason.unverified: Unverified finding in the latest analysis ({{n}})
rq.reason.moderate: Moderate finding in the latest analysis ({{n}})
rq.reason.noAnalysis: Medicines on record, no analysis yet
rq.reasons.label: Reasons this patient is listed
rq.error: Could not load the review queue.
rq.warn.followups: The follow-up list could not be loaded, so overdue and open follow-ups may be missing from this order.
rq.warn.failed: The analysis history of {{n}} patient(s) could not be read, so they are not placed in the order:
rq.summary: {{flagged}} patients with at least one flag · {{clear}} with no flag raised by these rules
rq.empty: No patients yet. Add a patient to start.
rq.clear.title: Patients with no flag ({{n}})
rq.clear.hint: No rule applied. This is not a safety statement.
